notes: Acute causes first: infection is the usual driver even with cancer or COPD coded.
Knaus lists poisoning under respiratory failure; an overdose sequenced first still gets Drug overdose.
After acute causes: respiratory failure in a cancer patient is usually infectious, so lung cancer with pneumonia is likely underpredicted.
Any COPD code (stable COPD with respiratory failure is usually an uncoded exacerbation, and COPD is less protective than the Respiratory fallback); bronchiolitis obliterans (J44.81) is not COPD.
Asthma with exacerbation or status asthmaticus only, plus anaphylaxis/angioedema: stable asthma would get the most protective weight in the table.
Same weight as when the GI bleed is sequenced first.
Acute coronary syndrome only (MI, unstable angina); chronic ischemic heart disease does not count.
Acute or acute-on-chronic heart failure only.
Ventricular tachycardia, fibrillation or flutter only; atrial fibrillation and other chronic rhythms do not count.
